root_cause.text: In crypto/af_alg.c, af_alg_pull_tsgl reused the old loop logic after adding page reassignment, so it reassigned a page to the destination scatterlist even when the remaining page length `plen` was zero, causing an off-by-one scatterlist/page reassignment overflow.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (dst)` to `if (dst && plen)` inside `af_alg_pull_tsgl`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that “the original loop wasn't updated so it may try to reassign one more page than necessary.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent zero-length scatterlist entries from being added to the destination list in af_alg_pull_tsgl.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the destination scatterlist update was changed from `if (dst)` to `if (dst && plen)`, and the accompanying comment was updated from `reassign page to dst after offset` to `reassign page to dst`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now skips creating a destination scatterlist entry when the computed segment length `plen` is zero, preventing insertion of zero-length SG entries and avoiding an unnecessary page reference increment for empty segments.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent zero-length scatterlist entries from being added to the destination list in af_alg_pull_tsgl.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the root cause: avoiding zero-length scatterlist entries in af_alg_pull_tsgl prevents the erroneous page reassignment when plen is zero, which is the off-by-one scatterlist/page reassignment overflow described.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct vulnerable operation: it reassigns a page into the destination scatterlist using plen even when plen is zero, creating a zero-length entry and causing the off-by-one scatterlist/page reassignment overflow.
Incrementing the destination scatterlist index unconditionally after the reassignment advances the entry count even for a zero-length plen case, embodying the off-by-one overflow condition.
This participates in the erroneous reuse/reassignment path by taking a page reference even when no valid destination entry should be created because plen is zero.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the core vulnerable statement: it assigns a page into the destination scatterlist using `plen` without ensuring `plen` is non-zero. When `plen` is zero, it creates an invalid zero-length destination entry and triggers the off-by-one scatterlist/page reassignment overflow described in the root cause.

This unconditional increment advances the destination scatterlist index even when the preceding reassignment used a zero `plen`, turning the zero-length insertion into an off-by-one overflow in destination entry accounting.
This statement is part of the same erroneous reassignment path, taking a page reference even in the zero-`plen` case where no destination scatterlist entry should be created.

The diff directly shows the relevant logic in af_alg_pull_tsgl, so it is sufficient to determine the presence/absence of the vulnerable construct. The root cause is specifically that the old loop logic could still reassign a page to the destination scatterlist when the remaining page length `plen` was zero, due to offset-based reassignment logic. In this commit, that vulnerable offset-based logic is removed from `af_alg_pull_tsgl`: the function signature changes from `af_alg_pull_tsgl(..., struct scatterlist *dst, size_t dst_offset)` to `af_alg_pull_tsgl(..., struct scatterlist *dst)`, and the body deletes the `dst_offset` handling block:

- removed: `if (dst_offset >= plen) { ... } else { get_page(page); sg_set_page(dst + j, page, plen - dst_offset, sg[i].offset + dst_offset); ... }`
- added: `get_page(page); sg_set_page(dst + j, page, plen, sg[i].offset); j++;`

Because the code no longer performs offset-based page reassignment using `plen - dst_offset`, the specific vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent. The companion change to `af_alg_count_tsgl` also removes the `offset` parameter and its offset-walking logic, consistent with the fix. Therefore this function does not contain the bug, and it already contains the fix.
